F.A.Q. CALL XLII CYCLE
APPLICATION
1.​ I entered incorrect data or have additional documents to include in the application; can I edit
it?
It is possible to modify the data or attach new documents as long as you have not started the signing
procedure, and only within the deadline of the call.
If you have already started the signing procedure, it is necessary to complete it, withdraw the application by
accessing the withdrawal procedure from the PICA dashboard, and submit a new application, within the
deadline set by the call. To submit a new application the previous application has to be correctly withdrawn.
2.​ Can I apply for admission to more than one Doctoral Course?
Yes, it is possible. Candidates who want to apply for more than one Course must submit as many
applications as the number of Courses they have chosen.
For the PhD Courses in Economics and Management, Industrial Engineering, Molecular Sciences, Social
Sciences, you can only apply for one curriculum. For each application, it is necessary to make a
non-refundable payment of € 30,00.
3.​ Do I need to have already contacted a supervisor before applying for admission?
It is not necessary; in general, the supervisor will be assigned by the Academic Board within four months
from the beginning of the courses. It is possible that some scholarships with bound research topics are linked
to a specific supervisor. Please check the information sheet of each PhD course.
4.​ Can I apply if I have a foreign degree? And what documents should I attach to the application
to request its eligibility evaluation?
Yes, candidates with a qualification obtained abroad may also participate, provided they meet the
requirements set out in the Selection Notice and submit in the last page of the application all required
documentation for the purpose of assessing eligibility, that is:
●​ In case of qualifications obtained in countries outside the European Union:
o​ diploma and transcript of records/certificate listing the examinations taken, with certified
translations into Italian or English;
o​ if already available, also the Declaration of Value issued by the relevant Italian embassies
and consulates or, alternatively, the Certificates of Comparability and Verification issued by
the Italian ENIC_NARIC centre – CIMEA;
●​ In case of qualifications obtained in European Union countries:
o​ diploma and Diploma Supplement, in Italian or English (as an alternative to the Diploma
Supplement, the Certificates of Comparability and Verification issued by the Italian
ENIC_NARIC centre – CIMEA).
●​ In case of qualifications yet to be awarded from countries outside the European Union:
o​ a diploma and a transcript of records/certificate listing the examinations taken, together with
certified translations into Italian or English, for the first-cycle degree;
o​ a certificate of enrolment in the university programme and a transcript of records/certificate
listing the examinations taken up to the date of submission of the application for this
selection notice;
●​ In case of qualifications yet to be awarded from European Union countries:
o​ diploma and Diploma Supplement, in Italian or English, for the first-cycle degree;

o​ certificate of enrolment in the university programme and transcript of records/certificate

5.​ Do I need to already hold a visa in order to apply?
No, you do not need to hold a visa at the time of application. If you are admitted, you will be required to
initiate the visa application process and apply for a residence permit at a later stage.
For further information regarding visas and residence permits, you may contact SAOS (Immigration Support
Service) at: saos@unipd.it
.
The International PhD Guide containing useful information is also available at:
https://www.unipd.it/dottorato/phd-guide
6.​ Do I need to know English or Italian?
For most courses, the exam can be carried in Italian, or English only. Many courses also include the
language assessment of English proficiency and, if applicable, a second foreign language.
You must consult the Course Information Sheet of your chosen programme for specific
requirements.
Please note that some PhD programmes are taught in Italian, the full list is available at:
https://www.unipd.it/en/dottorato/elenco
7.​ I have an employment contract; can I apply for admission to the Doctoral Courses?
Yes, however, admission to a Ph.D. implies an exclusive, full-time commitment. The Academic Board of
each Doctoral Program is in charge of deciding the compatibility between an employment contract and the
PhD career, after the candidate's enrollment.
The PhD programme can provide for positions with or without scholarship:
●​ In the latter case, the scholarship is granted exclusively to those who do not have, in the tax years of
predominant use of the scholarship, an annual gross income exceeding the amount of €17.443, as
provided for in Article 11 of the Call for Admission 2026/2027;
●​ In the latest case, work and PhD are compatible, but the Academic Board’s approval is necessary.
Exceeding the income limit results in the loss of the right to the scholarship for the year in which the income
event incompatible with the scholarship occurred.
8.​ When is my application valid?
From an administrative point of view, the application is valid when:
●​ a valid identity document has been attached;
●​ the non-refundable application fee of €30 has been paid;
●​ the application has been signed (if you log in using SPID or CIE, the application is automatically
signed).
Please note that you must also attach the documents specified in the Selection Notice and in the details of
each course.
9.​ Will I receive an email confirmation if the application process has been successful?
Yes, you will get an email confirming that your application has been received by the pica.cineca platform. If
you do not find the email in your inbox, please check the spam box. The email also contains the password to
view the intermediate results.
10.​ Can I request accommodation during the application process?
Yes, you can request accommodation at the "Casa dell’Assistente Prof. Virgilio Ducceschi" and/or at the
Galilean School of Advanced Studies (SGSS). For further accommodation options, please see the dedicated
section ("Housing") in the PhD Guide.
11.​ What requirements are needed to compete for a position as a "Doctoral Student" for the
Galilean School of Advanced Studies (SGSS)?

No specific requirements are needed: all candidates may express their interest in applying for these positions
by indicating it in the appropriate section. Following the selection procedure, those who will have achieved
the highest score in the ranking of each Doctoral Course and have requested to compete for a position
offered by the SGSS during the application process will take an admission test to enter the SGSS. The test
consists of an online oral interview, in which the candidate's motivations for becoming a Galilean student will
be evaluated, together with the doctoral research project and the contribution that the candidate intends to
make to the life of the SGSS.
12.​ Can I make the application payment with a credit/debit card that is not in my name?
Yes, there is no difference for payment purposes.
ADMISSION, RANKING, ENROLMENT
13.​ Where can I find the names of the members of the Selection Committees?
The Selection Committees are appointed after the deadline of the Call for Admission. To request the names
of the Committee members, send an email to the address listed in the information sheet of the PhD course.
14.​ I cannot participate on the day and at the time of the examination. Who do I contact?
You should refer to the administrative contact of the PhD Course you are applying for: the contact details are
available in the information sheet of the Doctoral Course.
15.​ Where can I find the results of admission tests?
The results of the admission tests will be published on the website indicated in the information sheet of the
specific PhD Course. You will be asked to enter a password, contained in the automatic email which was
sent by the PICA platform at the time of your application submission.
16.​ What are the key deadlines for the application process?
●​ Applications must be submitted by 20 May 2026 at 1:00 p.m. (Italian time, GMT+1)
●​ Reference letters by 25 May 2026 at 1:00 p.m. (Italian time, GMT+1)
●​ Entry examinations will take place between 4 June and 23 June 2026 (please refer to the individual
Course Information Sheets for specific dates).
●​ Final rankings will be published from 1 July 2026 and will be available at the following page:
https://www.unipd.it/en/dottorato/dottorati-42-ciclo
●​ The enrolment deadline is 23 July 2026; along with the publication of the rankings, enrolment
procedures will be available.
The dates indicated in the Call for Admission and in the individual Course information sheets constitute
official notice for all purposes; therefore, candidates will not receive any separate notification or
personal communication regarding the examination schedule. Candidates admitted to the Courses are
responsible for checking the dates and enrolment procedures.
17.​ In the ranking I was found eligible but not winner. What does this mean?
It means that you may be offered one of the vacant places in case of explicit or tacit withdrawal by winners.
The timing and instructions for replacements are ruled by artt. 7 and 10 of the Call for Admission to PhD
Courses.
18.​ What should I do if I have applied and have been admitted to more than one Doctoral Course?
In the event of a successful placement in more than one ranking, you can enrol in only one PhD Course. The
decision of which Course to enrol in is up to the candidate.

SCHOLARSHIPS, PAYMENTS, TUITION FEES
19.​ What is the PhD scholarship amount?
This year the PhD scholarship amount has been increased compared to the previous year and is now set at
€17,443 gross per year.
For the following programmes, the amount is furtherly increased and is now €18,643 gross per year:
Animal and food science; Astronomy; Biomedical Sciences; Biosciences; Clinical and Experimental
Sciences; Crop science; Developmental Medicine and Health Planning Sciences; Geosciences; Industrial
engineering; Information engineering; Land, environment, resources, health; Materials science and
technology; Mechatronics and Product Innovation Engineering; Molecular Medicine; Molecular sciences;
Pharmacological Sciences; Physics; Sciences of Civil, Environmental and Architectural Engineering;
Statistical Sciences; Veterinary Science and Food Safety.
20.​ How are PhD scholarships assigned?
PhD scholarships are assigned according to the ranking order that will be drawn up for each Course (or for
each curriculum, in the case in which the Course is announced by curriculum) and based on what is
indicated in art. 7 of the Call for Admission 2026/2027 to PhD Courses.
21.​ How does the allocation of places and scholarships in the ranking work?
Allocation is based on the preferences expressed in PICA at the time of application and follows the order of
ranking score. If, in the question "Are you applying for scholarships?":
●​ If you selected "No, I apply exclusively for places without scholarship", you may only be assigned a
place without scholarship (if available).
●​ If you selected "Yes", you primarily compete for places with scholarship; however, if places with
scholarship have already been assigned to higher-ranked candidates, you may be assigned a place
without scholarship (if available); in this case, you may decide whether to accept or decline.
●​ If you selected "Yes" and indicated one or more places with scholarships bound to specific research
topics: if you are assigned a place with scholarship bound to a specific research topic, not accepting
it results in exclusion from the ranking; if you are not assigned a place with scholarship bound to a
specific research topic, you will still compete for places with unbound scholarship.
22.​ Is the scholarship compatible with other sources of income?
The scholarship is awarded exclusively to those who do not have, in the tax years in which the scholarship is
mainly received, a gross annual income greater than the amount of one annual scholarship. However, the
cumulation of the doctoral scholarship with the following is not permitted:
●​ other scholarships awarded for any reason, except those awarded by national, international or
foreign institutions, that would be useful for integrating the doctoral activity with stays abroad;
●​ the financial treatment paid to doctors in medical Specialization courses. The payment of the
scholarship is suspended for the period of simultaneous enrolment in the medical Specialization
School;
●​ research grants. Those who benefit from research grants and win the PhD scholarship must
irrevocably renounce to one of them by the start date of the courses.
23.​ When will I receive the PhD scholarship?
The scholarship will be paid in monthly installments the 5th day of the following month, starting from the start
date of the course.
24.​ Can I start my PhD remotely if I have not yet obtained my visa?
Yes, for non-EU PhD candidates who require an entry visa for Italy, it is possible to start research activities
remotely for up to three months, subject to the positive approval of the PhD Programme Coordinator.
This option is granted upon proof that the visa application has been submitted to the relevant Embassy or
Consulate, which must be done immediately after completing the enrolment procedure.

The PhD scholarship is also paid during the remote period.
You are required to arrive in Italy no later than 31 January 2027.
25.​ Is a research budget provided for PhD students, and what is the amount?
Yes, a research budget is provided for each PhD student to support their research activities.
The total amount made available to PhD students for the entire duration of the programme is:
●​ €5,232.90 net for programmes with an annual scholarship of €17,443 (6.977,20€ for four-year
programmes).
●​ €5,292.90 net for programmes with an annual scholarship of €18,643 gross.
The activities that can be covered by the research budget are as follows:
1.Missions/travel;
2.Registration for conferences, seminars, etc.;
3.Consumable materials for research (e.g. chemical reagents, audiovisual supports, photocopies,
stationery...);
4.Publication costs;
5.Specific research-oriented training (e.g. language courses);
6.Books and articles, both in print and digital format;
7.IT research tools (software licences, etc.);
8.IT equipment in support of research (personal computers, tablets);
9.For PhD students with active or pending co-supervision agreements (cotutelle): tuition fees or other
administrative contributions required by the partner university.
26.​ Do those attending a PhD Course have to pay enrolment fees? Are there any fee waivers?
PhD students must pay annually for the regional tax for the right to study and stamp duty. It is possible to
request total or partial exemption from the payment, quantified as per the ISEE presented. For PhD students
with a scholarship, the quota for the aforementioned contribution will be withheld from the scholarship
payment.
EXCHANGE PERIOD ABROAD
27.​ Is it possible to carry out a research period abroad or in other institutions?
As reported in the University Regulation for PhD Courses, each PhD student is expected to carry out
research and training activities, consistent with the PhD project, at highly qualified institutions abroad. Always
in compliance with the aforementioned Regulation, PhD students can spend outside the administrative
headquarters of the PhD or the affiliated institutions a period that cannot exceed the half of the actual
duration of the Course.
Some PhD programs require a period abroad: please address the contact person of the PhD course you are
interested in.
Please note that the positions with a scholarship funded by the Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Padova e
Rovigo to carry out a PhD in cotutelle with one of the partner institutions of the Arqus Alliance, advertised in
the Call for Admission to PhD Course, require a mandatory period of stay abroad at the partner institution of
the cotutelle; the minimum duration varies depending on the project and it is reported in the information sheet
of the relevant Course.
WITHDRAWAL
28.​ What happens if you withdraw from the PhD program?
You can withdraw from the PhD program at any time using the specific form available here.
The monthly grant payments already received will not have to be returned, unlike those received following
withdrawal from studies.

Withdrawal is irrevocable and entails the end of the PhD studies, but does not exclude the possibility of
re-enrolment following the passing of the relevant admission tests. However, please note that anyone who
has already benefited from a PhD scholarship, even partially, cannot benefit from another one a second time.
​
TECHNICAL ISSUES
29.​ What to do if there are technical problems in the PICA platform?
For technical problems, it is necessary to contact IT technical support via the link at the bottom of the page
https://pica.cineca.it/unipd/dottorati42/, selecting the type of support requested and filling out the form. As the
application deadline approaches, system technical issues may arise due to overload, so we recommend
completing the application well in advance before the closing date.
